questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. The team's success was largely B. a result of it's coach's de dedication, C. a fact which they would all D. attest to.

options.text: a result of it's coach's dedication
a fact which they would all

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary error in the sentence is the use of the contraction "**it's**" instead of the possessive pronoun "**its**."
 
• "**It's**" is a contraction for "it is" or "it has," whereas "**its**" is used to show possession belonging to an inanimate object or a collective noun (like "the team").
 
• Additionally, there is a typographical error in the word "**de dedication**," which should simply be "dedication."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part B** (Option 2) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The team's success was largely **a result of its coach's dedication**, a fact which they would all attest to."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "The team's success was largely" **– This part correctly uses the possessive "team's" and the adverb "largely."
 
• **C: "a fact which they would all"** – This uses an appositive phrase and the relative pronoun "which" correctly to refer back to the preceding idea.
 
• **D: "attest to."** – The phrasal verb "attest to" means to provide evidence or serve as proof of something, which fits the context perfectly.
 
• **Common Confusion:** Many writers confuse *its* and *it's*. A quick tip is to replace the word with "it is"; if the sentence no longer makes sense, use "its."

questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. He has been B. to Italy, C. but he D. didn't went to Rome.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the past tense verb "**went**" following the auxiliary verb "**didn't**" (did not).
 
• In English grammar, when using the auxiliary verb "do," "does," or "did" for negation or questions, the main verb must always be in its **base form** (infinitive without "to").
 
• The auxiliary "did" already indicates the past tense, so using "went" creates an incorrect double-past construction.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part D** (Option 4) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He has been to Italy, but he **didn't go** to Rome."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "He has been"** – This uses the present perfect tense correctly to describe a life experience (visiting Italy).
 
• **B: "to Italy,"** – The preposition "to" is correctly used after "been" to indicate direction or destination.
 
• **C: "but he"** – This uses the coordinating conjunction "but" correctly to introduce a contrasting idea.
 
• **Verb Base Form:** Common examples of this rule include: *"He didn't **know**"* (not *knew*), *"She didn't **see**"* (not *saw*), and *"They didn't **come**"* (not *came*).

Which of the following sentences uses the word "bow" with the **same meaning** as in the following sentence?

"The performer took a deep bow to thank the audience"

options.text: She carefully tied the ribbon into a perfect bow.
He used the strong fishing line to make a tight bow.
The small gift was decorated with a large red bow.
The children were taught to bow to the queen as a sign of respect.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"bow"** is a homonym, meaning it has multiple meanings depending on context. In this sentence, it refers to bending the upper part of the body forward as a gesture of respect, acknowledgment, or greeting. (झुकना)

 
 
• **Example: **The performer took a deep bow to thank the audience for their applause.
 

 
• The correct sentence from the options that uses the word "bow" with the same meaning is: Option 4 - "The children were taught to bow to the queen as a sign of respect." Here, "bow" means to bend forward as an act of respect. (झुकना)

 
 
• **Example: **The children bowed gracefully to greet the queen.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

questions.question: What is the central contradiction discussed in the passage regarding digital surveillance?

options.text: The need for transparency vs. secrecy
The conflict between technological progress and personal privacy
The desire for security vs. the rights of corporations
The trade-off between national security and individual freedom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the central contradiction:***

 
 
• The very first sentence of the passage identifies the core issue as a "clear contradiction between the demands of modern security and the ideals of individual liberty."
 
• The second paragraph reinforces this theme by stating, "The underlying conflict, then, is how to balance personal privacy against national security."
 
• The passage focuses entirely on how the desire to keep nations safe (through surveillance) directly threatens the civil freedoms and privacy of individuals.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **The trade-off between national security and individual freedom.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (The need for transparency vs. secrecy)**: Incorrect. While an "open legal regime" is proposed as part of a solution, the fundamental problem driving the passage is security versus liberty, not just transparency versus secrecy.
 
• **Option 2 (The conflict between technological progress and personal privacy)**: Incorrect. The passage specifically pinpoints the "demands of modern security" as the opposing force to privacy, rather than just general technological progress.
 
• **Option 3 (The desire for security vs. the rights of corporations)**: Incorrect. The passage is concerned with the liberties and privacy of *citizens*. Corporations are mentioned as entities that, alongside governments, are capable of exercising surveillance, not as the victims losing their rights.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is a potential consequence of all-encompassing surveillance?

options.text: Suppression of dissent and freedom of expression

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the consequences of surveillance:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states: "All-encompassing surveillance has the potential to have a 'chilling effect' citizens, aware of being spied upon, might censor themselves, restrict their activism, and refrain from articulating dissen thus **suppressing the very dissent and freedom of expression** that are core to a healthy democracy."
 
• This clearly points to the negative impact that constant monitoring has on citizens, causing them to self-censor out of fear or suspicion.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Suppression of dissent and freedom of expression.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Increased political freedom)**: Incorrect because the passage argues the exact opposite—that surveillance compromises civil freedoms and suppresses core democratic practices.
 
• **Option 3 (Enhanced transparency in government operations)**: Incorrect because transparency is suggested in the second paragraph as a *solution* to balance security and privacy (via an "open legal regime"), rather than a result of the surveillance itself.
 
• **Option 4 (A reduction in government oversight)**: Incorrect because surveillance inherently represents a massive increase in monitoring and control over citizens, leading to a "surveillance state," not a reduction in oversight.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is necessary to protect citizens' privacy while maintaining national security?

options.text: A balanced legal regime with judicial supervision and public accountability
Limiting technology to only military applications
Complete transparency in government surveillance activities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the passage for solutions:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly addresses how to manage the conflict between personal privacy and national security in the second paragraph.
 
• It states: "A good balance is a strong and open legal regime that subjects surveillance a rigorous judicial supervision and public accountability."
 
• This highlights that the author does not want to completely abolish surveillance, but rather wants to control it through strict laws, oversight by judges, and accountability to the public.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **A balanced legal regime with judicial supervision and public accountability.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Total cessation of surveillance)**: Incorrect. The passage acknowledges there is a "genuine need governments to employ sophisticated technologies to respond to terrorism, organised crime, and other grave dangers," so it does not argue for completely stopping surveillance.
 
• **Option 3 (Limiting technology to only military applications)**: Incorrect. The passage does not suggest restricting technology to the military. In fact, it encourages technologies like "end-to-end encryption" for the public to protect private communication.
 
• **Option 4 (Complete transparency in government surveillance activities)**: Incorrect. While the passage advocates for an "open legal regime" and public discussion on "what data can be gathered," demanding *complete* transparency of all surveillance activities ignores the acknowledged need for national security operations against terrorism and crime. Option 2 is the exact balance proposed in the text.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the use of surveillance technologies by governments and corporations?

options.text: A beneficial tool for national security only
A means of societal control and political repression
A tool for promoting freedom of expression
A neutral force that has no impact on privacy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the passage:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly warns about the dangers of the vast data collected by these entities. It specifically highlights the "possibility of usir for political repression, social control, and targeting marginalised communities."
 
• It also notes that the ability of governments and corporations to exercise detailed surveillance leads to a "chilling effect" that suppresses democratic participation.
 
• This clearly aligns with the description of surveillance as a potential tool for widespread societal control and political repression.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **A means of societal control and political repression.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (A beneficial tool for national security only)**: Incorrect because while the passage acknowledges a "genuine need" for national security, it heavily emphasizes the severe threat surveillance poses to civil liberties, meaning it is not *only* beneficial.
 
• **Option 3 (A tool for promoting freedom of expression)**: Incorrect because the passage explicitly states the exact opposite: that surveillance suppresses "the very dissent and freedom of expression that are core to a healthy democracy."
 
• **Option 4 (A neutral force that has no impact on privacy)**: Incorrect because the central conflict discussed throughout the entire passage is the profound threat surveillance poses to personal privacy and individual liberty.

questions.question: In the passage, the word "chilling" most nearly means:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"chilling"** in the given context means causing great fear or apprehension; something that is frightening or intimidating. (डरावना या भयभीत करने वाला)

 
 
• **Example: **The chilling story made everyone unsettled.
 
 
 
• The closest synonym for **'chilling'** is **'intimidating'**, which means making someone feel frightened, scared or overawed. (डरावना)
 
 
• **Example: **The large shadow in the alley was quite intimidating.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Intimidating**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example: **The thrilling ride at the amusement park was very exciting.
 
 
 
• **Harmless** (नुकसान रहित): Not able or likely to cause harm.
 
 
• **Example: **The little puppy was harmless and friendly.
 
 
 
• **Invigorating** (ऊर्जावान): Making one feel strong, healthy, and full of energy.
 
 
• **Example: **A brisk walk in the morning is very invigorating.

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: A secret advantage** (गुप्त लाभ): Refers to a hidden or undisclosed benefit that someone has over others.

 

 
• **Example:** He had a secret advantage in the competition because he had trained with the best coach.

• **Example:** The company ensures all employees get the minimal legal benefits as per labor laws.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A medicine or other substance that has a calming or soothing effect.**

• The word **"Sedative"** refers to a medicine or substance that helps to calm or soothe the nerves or induces sleep. (शांत करने वाली दवा)

• **Example:** Coffee acts as a stimulant, keeping people awake and alert.
 
 
• Hence, the correct word is **"Sedative"**, which has a calming effect. (शांत प्रभाव)
 
 
• **Example:** After the stressful event, the patient was given a mild sedative to relax.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Sedative**.

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The old castle was believed to have been built by a legendary king.

options.text: A legendary king built the old castle, it was believed.
People believed that a legendary king had built the old castle.
The old castle had been built by a legendary king, it was believed.
A legendary king was believed to have built the old castle.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Complex Passive Structure:** The original sentence "The old castle was believed to have been built..." uses a double passive construction (a passive reporting verb "was believed" and a passive infinitive "to have been built").
 
• **Identify the Reporting Agent:** Since the sentence doesn't state who did the believing, we introduce a general subject like **"People"** or **"They"** to make the reporting verb active ("People believed").
 
• **Identify the Action Agent:** The agent of the building action is **"a legendary king."** In the active voice, he becomes the subject of the second clause.
 
• **Tense Alignment:** "To have been built" indicates an action that happened before the belief. Therefore, when converting to active, we use the **Past Perfect** ("had built") to show this sequence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"People believed that a legendary king had built the old castle."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "A legendary king built... it was believed." – This keeps the "it was believed" part in the passive voice.
 
• **Option 3:** "The old castle had been built..." – This remains in the passive voice.
 
• **Option 4:** "A legendary king was believed..." – This is still a passive construction focusing on the king rather than the act of believing.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

"Who is singing so beautifully?" the judge asked.

options.text: The judge asked who was singing so beautifully.
The judge asked who is singing so beautifully.
The judge asked who had been singing so beautifully.
The judge asked who singing so beautifully was.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** "Who is singing so beautifully?" the judge asked.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Sentence Structure (Interrogative to Assertive):**
 
 
• When converting a question into indirect speech, the sentence structure changes from interrogative (verb before subject) to assertive (subject before verb).
 
• The question format **"is singing"** becomes the statement format **"was singing."**
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Backshifting):**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb **"asked"** is in the past tense, the present continuous **"is singing"** shifts back to the past continuous **"was singing."**
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Connectors:**
 
 
• The question mark is removed.
 
• For 'Wh-' questions (who, what, where, etc.), the 'Wh-' word itself acts as the connector, so no additional conjunction like "that" or "if" is needed.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The judge asked who was singing so beautifully."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Fails to shift the tense from "is" to "was."
 
• **Option 3:** Uses the past perfect continuous ("had been singing"), which would only be correct if the original sentence was in the past continuous ("Who was singing?") or present perfect continuous ("Who has been singing?").
 
• **Option 4:** Uses an incorrect and awkward word order that does not follow standard English syntax for reported speech.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The dedicated researchers have already published the groundbreaking findings in a prestigious scientific journal.

options.text: The groundbreaking findings were already published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.
The groundbreaking findings have already been published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.
The groundbreaking findings have already published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.
The groundbreaking findings are already published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identify the Tense:** The active sentence "have already published" is in the **Present Perfect Tense**.
 
• **Passive Structure for Present Perfect:** The formula is **Object + has/have + been + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• **Step 1:** Identify the object "The groundbreaking findings" (plural) and make it the new subject.
 
• **Step 2:** Use the auxiliary verb **"have been"** to match the plural subject.
 
• **Step 3:** Maintain the adverb **"already"** between the auxiliary "have" and "been."
 
• **Step 4:** Include the agent "by the dedicated researchers" and the remaining prepositional phrase.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The groundbreaking findings have already been published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "were already published" – This is the Simple Past Passive, which removes the "have" (Present Perfect) aspect of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "have already published" – This is still an active construction but used with the object as the subject, which is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4:** "are already published" – This is the Present Simple Passive, which changes the completion aspect of the tense.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The historian asserted that the ruins were much older than previously thought and that new research had been continually proving it for years.

options.text: The historian said, "The ruins were much older than previously thought, and new research has been continually proving it for years."
The historian said, "The ruins are much older than previously thought, and new research has been continually proving it for years."
The historian said, "The ruins are much older than previously thought, and new research had been continually proving it for years."
The historian said, "The ruins were much older than previously thought, and new research had been continually proving it for years."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The historian asserted that the ruins were much older than previously thought and that new research had been continually proving it for years.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Tense Change (Forward-shifting):**
 
 
• When converting back to direct speech, we restore the speaker's original timeframe.
 
• The simple past **"were"** shifts forward to the simple present **"are,"** as the historian is stating a current fact or discovery.
 
• The past perfect continuous **"had been continually proving"** shifts forward to the present perfect continuous **"has been continually proving"** to reflect an action that started in the past and is still ongoing at the time of the assertion.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The formal reporting verb **"asserted"** is typically represented as **"said"** in direct speech options, followed by the specific quoted statement.
 
 
 
• **Contextual Clues:**
 
 
• The phrase **"for years"** combined with **"continually"** strongly implies the use of the Present Perfect Continuous in the original direct speech to show duration up to the present.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The historian said, 'The ruins are much older than previously thought, and new research has been continually proving it for years.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Uses the past tense ("were"), which makes the statement sound like the ruins are no longer old or the fact is disconnected from the present.
 
• **Option 3:** Correctly shifts the first verb but incorrectly leaves the second verb in the past perfect continuous ("had been"), which would imply the research stopped before the historian spoke.
 
• **Option 4:** Retains both past tenses from the indirect speech, failing to convert them to the speaker's original present perspective.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph. **

P. He spent his days in the lab, carefully scanning samples under a microscope.

Q. Dr. Alistair Finch was an accomplished biologist who specialized in the discovery of new species.

R. His peers would tease him that he looked more upon the microbial world than on the actual one.

S. His greatest find was from a small, ordinary pond deep in the Amazon rainforest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph is structured as a character introduction followed by his habits, the social perception of those habits, and a culminating achievement.
 
• **Sentence Q is the first sentence** because it introduces the protagonist, Dr. Alistair Finch, and establishes his professional background:
 
 
• "Dr. Alistair Finch was an accomplished biologist who specialized in the discovery of new species."
 
 
 
• **Sentence P follows** as it describes the day-to-day activities associated with the profession mentioned in the first sentence:
 
 
• "He spent his days in the lab, carefully scanning samples under a microscope."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the third sentence** because it provides a commentary on his behavior described in P, using the "microscope" context to explain the "microbial world" joke:
 
 
• "His peers would tease him that he looked more upon the microbial world than on the actual one."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the fourth sentence** as it shifts from his general routine to a specific, notable event that highlights his success in his field:
 
 
• "His greatest find was from a small, ordinary pond deep in the Amazon rainforest."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **QPRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Dr. Alistair Finch was an accomplished biologist who specialized in the discovery of new species. He spent his days in the lab, carefully scanning samples under a microscope. His peers would tease him that he looked more upon the microbial world than on the actual one. His greatest find was from a small, ordinary pond deep in the Amazon rainforest."

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. She repeatedly listened to the song, taking in its passion and rhythm.

Q. She made a sequence of motions and connected them to form a smooth flow.

R. Her artistic vision was brought to the stage by the dancers, who executed the work brilliantly.

S. She taught the dance to her troupe, refining each step and making sure every moment was synchronized.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph follows the creative process of choreography, moving from inspiration and creation to instruction and final performance.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it represents the initial stage of inspiration—understanding the music before any physical movement begins:
 
 
• "She repeatedly listened to the song, taking in its passion and rhythm."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** as the second stage, where the internal inspiration is translated into a physical sequence of choreography:
 
 
• "She made a sequence of motions and connected them to form a smooth flow."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the third sentence** because it describes the transition from the creator to the performers, involving teaching and synchronization:
 
 
• "She taught the dance to her troupe, refining each step and making sure every moment was synchronized."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the fourth sentence** as it provides the culmination of the entire process—the successful performance of the artistic vision on stage:
 
 
• "Her artistic vision was brought to the stage by the dancers, who executed the work brilliantly."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQSR**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"She repeatedly listened to the song, taking in its passion and rhythm. She made a sequence of motions and connected them to form a smooth flow. She taught the dance to her troupe, refining each step and making sure every moment was synchronized. Her artistic vision was brought to the stage by the dancers, who executed the work brilliantly."
